notes._: This file records WHICH GATE guards each entry of the authorization surface, not whether that gate is correct. It exists because the same question -- may this actor do this? -- is answered by more than twenty distinct idiom combinations in this repository, two of which (gated-lookup, ensure-helper) are indistinguishable from an ungated method in a diff. A NEW entry, or an entry whose gate disappears, blocks; confirming the gate and running --update is the deliberate look this check is asking for.
notes.gate:NONE: No named gate found. For most of these that is correct -- an avatar acting on its own avatar (dance, typing, posture, expression, sign, look-to) needs no authority beyond being in the room, which the avatar lookup already establishes. It is NOT automatically correct for anything that touches another player's property, currency, or the room's own settings. A new NONE is the one to read twice.
notes.gate:gated-lookup: The gate is inside a lookup: FindManipulableItemAsync(ctx, id) asks SecurityModule.CanManipulateFurniAsync and returns null when refused. It reads like _state.ItemsById.TryGetValue(id, out item), which asks nothing. One identifier apart, opposite meaning.
notes.gate:ensure-helper: A private static that throws -- EnsurePetOwner(ctx, pet) raises NoPermissionToManipulatePet. No return value, so nothing at the call site says a check happened.
notes.gate:IMPL-NOT-FOUND: The declared method's implementation was not resolved by name. Not a finding on its own -- it means this check cannot speak for that entry, which is worth knowing.
notes.grain:IRoomFurni.Edit.cs::ApplyFurniEdit: Deliberately gateless, and the file says so: 'the authorization question is answered once, by the caller, against room.furni.edit'. That contradicts ROOMG-GATE-038, stated in RoomSecurityModule, RoomGrain.Moderation and RoomGrain.Settings: 'a handler is not a security boundary... the grain is the one that decides'. Its one caller today (VortexApplyFurniEditMessageHandler) does check the capability. Nothing makes the next one.
notes.http:anonymous: /api/login, /api/logout and the asset routes are anonymous by design. /api/public/* is the public surface and is not listed as anonymous because it declares no gate at all -- which is the same thing, said less clearly.
notes._scope: Room grains, group grains, player grains, and every HTTP endpoint. Non-room grains were added after the groups system showed the same shape: fifteen methods on IGroupGrain and eight on IGroupForumGrain decide who may kick, promote, rename and moderate, and the rule the repository states -- callable by anything in the cluster that can name it -- never mentioned rooms.
notes.gate:gated-mutator: MutateAsAdminAsync(actor, group => { ... }) folds the check into a mutation wrapper that takes a lambda. The call site shows a lambda and an actor; it does not show a check. UpdateIdentity, UpdateColors and UpdateBadge all rely on it.
notes.gate:group-rank: IsAdminAsync, a GroupMemberRank comparison, or an inline OwnerPlayerEntityId != actorId.
notes.gate:permission-matrix: The forum's own matrix: Allows(settings.ModPermission, role), CanRead, PostPermission. A fourth vocabulary for the same question.
notes.grain:Groups/IGroupForumGrain.cs::Modera: Gated by LoadForModerationAsync, which returns (null, None) when the actor fails the matrix. Note the shape: it returns a TUPLE whose role the caller discards, so the call site reads like a plain load and the refusal rides on the group being null. ModerateMessageAsync and UpdateThreadAsync share it.
notes.grain:Groups/IGroupForumGrain.cs::StaffM: Takes a raw int actor and checks NOTHING. Its one production caller is the dashboard route, which requires Capabilities.Dashboard.OpsGuildsManage. Same shape as ApplyFurniEditAsync: correct today, guaranteed by nobody tomorrow.
notes.grain:Rooms/IRoomModeration.cs::SetHotel: Takes NO actor at all, so the grain cannot check even in principle -- a hotel-wide mute authorized entirely by its caller. ModMuteMessageHandler does resolve ModerationAction.Mute before calling. The parameter list is the finding: an actor that is not passed cannot be verified.
notes.grain:Groups/IGroupDirectoryGrain.cs: The entries here take a PlayerId that IS the subject -- your own favourites, your own read markers, your own memberships. No gate is needed, and SetFavouriteAsync still checks membership before letting you favourite. Same class as the avatar methods.
